protocol: Gearbox six states (3000 rpm/70% load) and rotor ten states (2400 rpm/20% load); each state 200 samples, randomly 160 train/40 test; ten repeats. Accuracy mean±SD; acoustic-only, IRT-only and five multimodal comparators. Rotor comparison adds -1 dB Gaussian noise (§4.1–4.2).
finding: Gearbox mean accuracy 99.54±0.54%, versus acoustic-only 88.63±1.43% and IRT-only 90.54±1.37% (Table2 p12). Fusion ablation: concatenation 92.76±1.53%, proposed 99.54±0.54% (Table8 p17). At -3 dB simultaneous Gaussian corruption, proposed 91.96±1.38% (Table9 p19).

title: Fault Diagnosis of Harmonic Drives Using Multimodal Collaborative Meta Network With Severely Missing Modality
modalities: Physical vibration acceleration plus servo-system signals (including current, speed, position/error/torque channels); no camera input (§II-A1, III-A).
fusion: Intermediate multimodal collaborative meta-network (MCMN): modality encoders, reconstruction from modal priors, uncertainty-based feature regularization, meta-learning/Monte Carlo optimization and classifier. Missing vibration can be reconstructed from available servo features (§II-A/B).
protocol: Custom industrial-robot harmonic-drive data with four health states. Servo samples split 7:3; vibration training counts 228/360/450/369 by state and 45 test samples/state (§III-B, p5). A→A, B→B, A&B→A and A&B→A&B compare servo-only, vibration-only, privileged training and full-input fusion. Test vibration availability is varied at 100/33/67/0% of servo sample count; training vibration availability at 25/50/75/100% is also studied (§IV-C3/D). Accuracy, comparative generative/classifier models and module ablations; independent repeated-run uncertainty not established.
finding: §IV-C2 p6 reports vibration-only accuracy 97.22%, full vibration+servo fusion 96.67%, and missing-vibration inference 89.44% versus servo-only 74.52%. Thus the reported complete-input fusion score is below the best reported unimodal score, while privileged multimodal training helps the retained servo input. Comparator architectures differ, and source reporting issues limit the interpretation.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—servo-only and vibration-only, full-input fusion, CNN/ResNet18, AE/AAE/GAN/DCGAN, and reconstruction/regularization ablations (§IV). Retained-input versus privileged-input costs differ; not a matched-capacity universal fusion ranking.

Uncertainty is used for regularization; calibration is not established.
limitations: Servo identity is inconsistent: §IV-C2 calls the 74.52% stream ATO, while §IV-C4 gives ATO 53.95% and TCCV 74.52%. Fig5 per-class values do not straightforwardly reconcile with prose overall accuracies; no alternative overall score calculated. Fault labels are tied to particular speed/load setups (§III-B), limiting condition-invariant conclusions. No held-out machine/run split, calibrated-uncertainty metric or physical deployment timing established.

title: The Eyecandies Dataset for Unsupervised Multimodal Anomaly Detection and Localization
modalities: Synthetic RGB, depth and surface-normal maps
fusion: Early channel concatenation into a convolutional autoencoder
protocol: Eyecandies 10 categories; defect-free train/validation, mixed test; RGB/RGBD/RGBDN reconstruction; image/pixel AUROC; Tables 2–3.
finding: §5 reports adding depth can reduce performance; adding normals improves almost every category.
baseline_appraisal: yes—RGB-only autoencoder; RGB feature-based baselines in Table 1.
robustness_appraisal: Multiple lighting renders supplied, not a verified sensor-dropout/noise/shift experiment.
limitations: Synthetic data; logical anomalies excluded; direct mapping to real lighting/noise robustness unproven. Conference 2022; Springer volume 2023.
read_version: Full CVF author PDF; §5 and Tables 2–3 read.

title: The MVTec 3D-AD Dataset for Unsupervised 3D Anomaly Detection and Localization
modalities: Registered RGB and 3D scans
fusion: Early RGB-channel/voxel augmentation in baseline models
protocol: 10 categories; 2656 training, 294 validation, 249 normal+948 anomalous test. 3D-only versus 3D+RGB; AU-PRO integration limit 0.3 and image ROC.
finding: §4.2: adding RGB improves localization except Variation Models.
baseline_appraisal: yes—3D/depth-only; RGB-only: NOT STATED in inspected benchmark.
robustness_appraisal: No dedicated missing/noisy/shift stress test identified.
limitations: Static inspection setting; coarse voxel baselines; natural invalid points are not injected modality dropout.
read_version: Full SCITEPRESS PDF; Table 1 and baseline setup/results read.

title: What Makes Training Multi-Modal Classification Networks Hard?
modalities: TRANSFERABLE (non-industrial)—RGB video, optical flow and audio
fusion: Late feature concatenation, intermediate/gated alternatives; adaptive gradient blending
protocol: Kinetics 240k train/20k validation used for testing; mini-Sports/mini-AudioSet and other tasks. Table 1 matches stream architectures; top-1 accuracy.
finding: Kinetics Table 1: naive audio+RGB 71.4% versus RGB-only 72.6%; three modalities 70.0%.
baseline_appraisal: yes—RGB-only, audio-only, optical-flow-only.
robustness_appraisal: Whole-modality missing/noisy/industrial shift tests: NOT STATED.
limitations: Non-industrial video classification; its late fusion is feature concatenation before a classifier, not independent decision voting.
read_version: Full CVF accepted PDF; Table 1 and §3 inspected.

title: Audio-visual cross-modality knowledge transfer for machine learning-based in-situ monitoring in laser additive manufacturing
modalities: Coaxial melt-pool camera and microphone audio
fusion: Data-level, feature-level and author-defined decision-level fusion; cross-modal semantic alignment/mapping alternatives
protocol: L-DED 4345 paired samples; 8:1:1 split (3476/434/435); Bayesian hyperparameter search; accuracy, AUROC, balanced accuracy. Camera-only/audio-only and three fusion schemes.
finding: §5.1: camera-only optimal accuracy 0.974; best fusion 0.982; audio→visual semantic alignment 0.986 with camera-only inference.
baseline_appraisal: yes—visual-only and audio-only.
robustness_appraisal: Yes—planned modality removal at inference and synthetic Gaussian visual/audio noise (§5.4.1); cross-machine shift: NOT STATED.
limitations: Read author preprint; final-version equivalence not established. Specimen/build-independent split not established. Author decision fusion concatenates representations immediately before prediction.
read_version: Full arXiv PDF; §3–5 read; metadata linked to published Additive Manufacturing article.

title: Deep convolutional neural networks for cyclic sensor data
modalities: Hydraulic pressure, flow, temperature, electrical power and vibration sensors
fusion: Early raw-input fusion versus per-sensor CNN feature concatenation (called late sensor fusion by authors)
protocol: ZeMA hydraulic testbed; random 70/10/20 split; accumulator classification; 50 tuning iterations; single-sensor and sensor-pair ablations, repeated tuning.
finding: §III: all-sensor CNN error 20.5% versus best single-sensor PS1 1.7%; conventional 17-sensor baseline 1%. Adding uniform-noise channel to PS1 gives 30.3% error.
baseline_appraisal: yes—individual sensor CNNs and conventional multi-sensor baseline.
robustness_appraisal: Yes—irrelevant uniform-noise input; missing/shifted modalities: NOT STATED.
limitations: Preprint; random-cycle split and tuning-resource constraints; per-sensor feature concatenation differs from independent decision fusion.
read_version: Full arXiv v1 PDF/HTML read; no published conference DOI confirmed.

title: Towards Total Recall in Industrial Anomaly Detection
modalities: RGB inspection images
fusion: Unimodal baseline; patch-feature memory bank and coreset subsampling
protocol: MVTec AD 15 categories; nominal-only train and mixed test; image/pixel AUROC and PRO; comparisons to strong visual baselines and few-shot trials.
finding: Abstract reports image AUROC up to 99.6% on MVTec AD.
baseline_appraisal: yes—visual-only method itself.
robustness_appraisal: Missing/noisy/shifted multimodal tests: NOT STATED.
limitations: This paper is a visual-only baseline, not a test of visual+sensor fusion; read arXiv author version.
read_version: Full arXiv PDF; methods and experimental protocol read.

title: MVTec AD — A Comprehensive Real-World Dataset for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
modalities: Industrial RGB images only; no aligned machine-sensor modality.
fusion: No multimodal fusion; visual anomaly-detection benchmark/unimodal reference.
protocol: MVTec AD: 15 categories, 3629 normal train/validation and 1725 test images (§3). Six visual approaches; classification/segmentation ROC-AUC and per-region overlap (§4).
finding: §4.4: no method consistently succeeds across categories; high ROC-AUC can coexist with poor thresholded region overlap.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—visual-only autoencoders, AnoGAN, CNN feature dictionary, texture inspection and variation model.
robustness_appraisal: No controlled missing/noisy/shifted multimodal trial; defects are target anomalies, not modality corruptions.
limitations: Useful visual-only benchmark, not evidence of aligned multimodal benefit or sensor-failure resilience.
read_version: Official CVPR 2019 proceedings PDF

title:
MIMII Dataset: Sound Dataset for Malfunctioning Industrial Machine
                        Investigation and Inspection
modalities: Eight-channel machine audio; valves, pumps, fans and slide rails; real-factory background noise.
fusion: Acoustic-only autoencoder baseline; multiple microphones are not heterogeneous physical modalities.
protocol: Per-machine/model-ID normal-only training; all abnormal segments and equally many randomly selected normal segments test; log-mel AE, 50 epochs, AUC mean of three runs; SNR +6/0/-6 dB (§4).
finding: Table3 fan mean AUC .94/.84/.70 at +6/0/-6 dB; valve .67/.61/.53. Explicit acoustic-noise degradation supports a unimodal robustness comparator.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—acoustic-only AE.
robustness_appraisal: Noise: yes, measured factory-background mixing at three SNR levels. Missing/held-out-domain shift: not established.
limitations: No camera+sensor comparison or missing-modality test. Separate per-ID models do not establish unseen-machine generalization.
read_version: Official DCASE 2019 proceedings PDF; primary author header reconfirmed Kenji Ichige

title: ToyADMOS: A Dataset of Miniature-Machine Operating Sounds for Anomalous Sound Detection
modalities: Four-channel miniature-machine audio plus recorded factory environmental noise; toy car, conveyor and train.
fusion: Audio AE baseline; train channels mixed to one observation, not a visual/sensor fusion study.
protocol: Case1: 1000 randomly selected normal IND samples train; remaining normal/anomalous samples test; noise mixing and 16kHz audio; log-mel AE (§4).
finding: §4 baseline AUROC .874/.981/.843 for car/conveyor/train; controlled noise mixing is described, not a multimodal advantage.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—audio-only AE.
robustness_appraisal: Noise: explicit environmental-noise mixing with fixed scaling. Missing/cross-machine shift: not established.
limitations: Miniature-machine proxy; read accepted arXiv manuscript, not VOR. No physical camera inputs or sensor-dropout experiment.
read_version: arXiv accepted WASPAA 2019 manuscript

title: Description and Discussion on DCASE2020 Challenge Task2: Unsupervised Anomalous Sound Detection for Machine Condition Monitoring
modalities: Mono noisy operating sounds from six machine types; ToyADMOS/MIMII-derived task data.
fusion: Audio-only AE baseline and discussion of challenge classifiers/ID conditioning; no paired camera branch.
protocol: DCASE2020 Task2: around1000 normal train samples per machine-ID, 100–200 each normal/anomalous development tests; AUC and pAUC up to FPR .1; ten baseline trials (§2–3).
finding: Table1 fan ID0 baseline AUC 54.41±.47%, slide-rail ID0 96.19±.43%; task difficulty varies substantially. §4.3 notes similar operating sounds across IDs can cause training failure.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—audio-only AE; machine-ID training/classification approaches discussed.
robustness_appraisal: Noise present in supplied recordings. Missing input and source→target shift experiments: not established by this 2020 paper.
limitations: 2020 task is not the later source/target domain-shift challenge. Published workshop text read while exported DOI identifies arXiv record; version equivalence unverified.
read_version: Official DCASE2020 workshop PDF linked to the exported arXiv record

title: A Novel Cross-Domain Mechanical Fault Diagnosis Method Fusing Acoustic and Vibration Signals by Vision Transformer
modalities: Acoustic and vibration signals
fusion: Feature-level self-attention fusion in parallel vision-transformer branches; adversarial/Wasserstein domain alignment
protocol: Custom 6205 bearing rig; five states; cross-speed and cross-load transfer with labeled source/unlabeled target. Accuracy versus TCA, FTNN, WD-DTL; exact split sizes: NOT STATED.
finding: §4.2 reports average cross-speed accuracy above 98%; §4.3 also notes degradation for large domain differences.
baseline_appraisal: NOT STATED
robustness_appraisal: Yes—operating-condition shift; missing/noisy stress tests: NOT STATED.
limitations: Source prose is internally inconsistent about some task comparisons; no strong unimodal ablation verified. A vision transformer on signal images is not a physical camera modality.
read_version: Publisher full HTML; methods and cross-speed/load results read.

title: A Deep-Learning-Based Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion Approach for Detection of Equipment Faults
modalities: Vibration and motor current; raw series and STFT representations
fusion: Heterogeneous feature-level fusion across sensors and derived signal domains
protocol: Paderborn condition 1 only; ESOGU custom bearing rig. PU 70/15/15 and ESOGU 10000/1000/1000; unchanged partitions across input trials; accuracy mean±SD over five trials.
finding: Four-input mean accuracy 97.10% PU and 100% ESOGU; sensor/domain ablations reported.
baseline_appraisal: yes—current-only and vibration-only combinations.
robustness_appraisal: No missing/noisy/shift stress test identified; PU uses only one operating condition.
limitations: Within-condition sample partitions do not establish cross-machine or cross-condition generalization. STFT images are derived representations, not camera observations.
read_version: Publisher full HTML; §5.2–6 and input-combination protocol read.

title: Multisensor fusion-based digital twin for localized quality prediction in robotic laser-directed energy deposition
modalities: Coaxial melt-pool camera + microphone + off-axis SWIR thermal camera; robot TCP position aligns features to part location.
fusion: Early spatiotemporal feature fusion, ROS synchronization and supervised classifiers; NN selected from seven models.
protocol: Stratified 8:2 random train/test, five runs mean/SD; grid-search 10-fold CV (§3.6/4.1). Accuracy, ROC-AUC and false-alarm rate; acoustic-only, vision-only, thermal-only models.
finding: NN fusion accuracy 95.6% (Fig15/§4.1; abstract rounds to 96%); authors report fusion exceeds individual sensing approaches.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—vision-only, acoustic-only and thermal-only.
robustness_appraisal: Missing/noisy/shifted: no explicit controlled failure/shift protocol established; production surroundings alone do not establish robustness.
limitations: Random location/time-point split does not establish held-out-build generalization; adjacent observations may be dependent. Dataset count differs: 292,200 in training description versus 29,200 in §4.1. Manuscript-to-VOR equivalence not verified.
read_version: Complete author-uploaded 37-page manuscript read in ResearchGate HTML; PDF download unavailable

title: A feature-level multi-sensor fusion approach for in-situ quality monitoring of selective laser melting
modalities: Physical airborne acoustic emission (microphone) + photodiode light-intensity signals, both sampled at 10 kHz. CNN images are signal-to-image encodings, not camera/video input; optical microscopy and density measurements provide quality labels (§2–3).
fusion: Intermediate/feature-level concatenation of two CNN branches after parallel convolution/pooling, followed by further convolution/pooling and fully connected classification (§3.3, Fig8, PDF pp8–9).
protocol: Custom 316L SLM data: 15 process settings, 45 cubes/255 captured layers; three quality classes based on porosity and relative density. Overlapping track-step signal windows converted to 64×64 images; per-class random 80/20 train/test split (60,424/15,107 images), plus random ten-fold CV. Same optimizer/training hyperparameters used for compared methods. Accuracy and per-image classification time; acoustic-only and photodiode-only variants and eight alternative architectures (§4, PDF pp9–12).
finding: Table3 (PDF p12): proposed CNN fusion accuracy 99.08%, versus acoustic-only 95.82% and photodiode-only 96.06%. Ten-fold means: fusion 98.35%, acoustic 96.02%, photodiode 95.64% (PDF p11). Direct negative examples in Table3: LeNet-5 fusion 90.71% < photodiode 91.04%; RNN fusion 88.24% < photodiode 92.43%; LSTM fusion 90.35% < acoustic 92.13%. These show architecture-dependent fusion benefits within this experiment.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—CNN-AE acoustic-only and CNN-PH photodiode-only; Table3 gives single-sensor and fusion columns for all nine listed architectures, including negative fusion results.
robustness_appraisal: Missing: no whole-modality failure experiment established. Noise: 4 kHz high-pass filtering of ambient acoustic noise is preprocessing, not a quantified SNR/noise-stress evaluation. Shift: multiple process settings are pooled; held-out new-process-condition/build transfer is left for future work (§5).
limitations: Random splits are at encoded-window/image level after overlapping windows are formed; shared signal content and same-part observations can cross folds, so independent build/part generalization is not established (audit inference). Modal data are explicitly not registered (§3.2). Labels summarize part-quality categories, not localized pore ground truth. No confidence intervals or seed-repeat uncertainty established. Different architectures complicate comparisons beyond matched single-input variants. Future new-process testing is proposed, not completed.
read_version: User-supplied publisher version, Journal of Manufacturing Processes 84 (2022), pp913–926, 14 PDF pages.

title: Multi-modal sensor fusion with machine learning for data-driven process monitoring for additive manufacturing
modalities: Physical layerwise EO camera imagery (six pre/post-scan/flash views) + microphone acoustics + two photodiode multispectral-emission channels (520/532 nm) + machine laser scan-vector/log-derived variables. Fifteen input channels include multiple views and derived metrics, not fifteen independent physical sensor types. Post-build CT supplies labels, not an inference input (§2.1–2.3).
fusion: Intermediate hidden-layer concatenation: modality-specific 605→24 sigmoid encoders, then a shared fully connected binary output; synchronized temporal signals rasterized onto the camera/build grid before feature extraction (§2.2–2.4, Figs7–10).
protocol: One Ti6Al4V cylinder on a ProX320; 32,352 flaw voxels and 136,222 nominal voxels from OEM-parameter regions. Four-fold random voxel CV, 75/25 train/test, with overlapping 300 μm local 3D neighborhoods. Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, FPR/FNR and ROC-AUC. Retrained truncated networks evaluate individual modalities and subsets (§2.3–3.2).
finding: All-channel voxel test accuracy .9854, precision .9371, recall .9904, F1 .9630 (Table2, PDF p10). Sensitivity results: fused EO imagery AUC >.97; individual scan metrics .52–.61 but fused scan metrics >.9; acoustic/MS around .75 with no significant gain from combining them (§3.2, p11). On one naturally imbalanced layer at threshold .5, accuracy .9921 accompanies precision .2487 (Table3)—high accuracy alone obscures false positives.
baseline_appraisal: Yes—individual camera views, emission channels and scan-vector metrics, plus retrained subsets/all-modalities; modality contribution rather than an equal-parameter early-versus-late architecture benchmark (§3.2, Figs16–17).
robustness_appraisal: Missing: planned channel subsets retrained for sensitivity; no unexpected inference-time dropout test. Noise/shift: altered lighting/background noise and new parts/builds are identified for future work (§5), not controlled robustness experiments in the reported validation.
limitations: Only one part/build; random neighboring-voxel splits and overlapping feature neighborhoods permit spatial dependence across folds (audit inference), so cross-build generalization is not established. Training/evaluation subset uses approximately4:1 nominal/flaw sampling; naturally imbalanced deployment differs. Microphone rate is inconsistent: 192 kHz on PDF p3 versus250 kHz on p4. Authors explicitly defer multi-part/build and noise/lighting transfer validation to future work. AUC discussion uses rounded/graph values, not claimed exact measurements.
read_version: User-supplied publisher version, Additive Manufacturing 48 (2021), article102364, 13 PDF pages.

title: Deep learning-based monitoring of laser powder bed fusion process on variable time-scales using heterogeneous sensing and operando X-ray radiography guidance
modalities: Acoustic emission + three optical photodiode channels (back-reflection, visible, infrared). Operando X-ray images guide labels, not a camera branch supplied to the classifier.
fusion: Early synchronized multichannel signal tensor into hybrid CNN-LSTM; hybrid refers to neural architecture, not proven early+late fusion.
protocol: 316L mini-LPBF, three processing regimes; non-overlapping .83/1.65/2.5/3.30 ms windows; stochastic 70/30 split and unseen-duration tests (§3.3–4). Per-class confusion matrices and saliency.
finding: Table5 includes per-class values 97.7–100%; Table6 unseen-duration values include 95.9%. Saliency identifies informative channels but does not measure a unimodal performance gap.
baseline_appraisal: NOT STATED—channel saliency, not a strong acoustic-only/optical-only performance comparison.
robustness_appraisal: Shift: unseen input-window durations only. Missing/added noise/cross-machine shift: not established.
limitations: Abstract/results prose and confusion-table numbers differ; preserve table-specific claims. Window-duration generalization is not cross-machine transfer. No independent unimodal performance comparator established; X-ray guidance must not be counted as an inference modality.
read_version: DORA institutional repository publisher-version PDF, CC BY

title: Heterogeneous sensor data fusion for multiscale, shape agnostic flaw detection in laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing
modalities: Three thermo-optical imaging sources: spatter camera, NIR tomography camera, recoater camera. No independent vibration/current/acoustic input.
fusion: Early fusion of graph spectral-radius features and mean melt-pool intensity into KNN/SVM/ANN/logistic regression; EWMA for geometry errors.
protocol: 66 parts across three builds. Balanced porosity samples, random 80/20 split, 10-fold CV/Bayesian tuning, ten trials; independent third build with rotated layout/changed power schedule (§3.5/4.4). F-score/FPR/FNR.
finding: Table4 SVM pore-severity F-score 93.5±1.68%; §4.4 third-build porosity false-positive rate <1.5%. Cross-geometry warpage model transfer shown (Fig21).
baseline_appraisal: Feature sufficiency/plots discussed, but controlled matched single-camera performance comparison not established.
robustness_appraisal: Shift: changed build layout/process schedule and cone-to-overhang transfer. Missing/added sensor noise: no controlled trials established.
limitations: Validation build lacks substantial porosity; authors explicitly require further testing to estimate false negatives and F-score. Sample counts disagree between §3.5 and Table4; avoid deriving denominators. No matched all-versus-single-camera score table established.
read_version: Virginia Tech repository publisher PDF
